summary: Echoes of Exploration brings NASA's retired hardware back to life for school-age children. Seventeen machines left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space, from Apollo's lunar modules and rovers to Viking, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, Dawn and Kepler, appear as ghosts on an interactive map and a clickable 3D Moon and Mars. Children open a mission page with real NASA photos and verified facts, then chat with the spacecraft in its own voice at two reading levels, with voice input and read-aloud. A fact-grounded AI answers only from NASA mission pages and shows its source under every answer, so the science stays accurate. It is a website that installs like a phone app, works offline, and adds new missions by editing data, not code. Security is built in: protected keys, rate limits and defenses against prompt injection.
details:
Echoes of Exploration is an interactive educational web application developed to make space exploration more engaging and easier to understand, especially for younger learners. The project focuses on the stories of historic spacecraft and their contributions to space exploration. Instead of presenting mission information through articles alone, the website allows users to explore the Moon, Mars and deep space while discovering the spacecraft that travelled there.

The platform features 17 mission profiles covering different spacecraft missions. Users can browse them through an interactive map or mission grid and open individual mission pages to learn about their history, achievements and important facts. Another key feature is the 3D planetary environment, where users can rotate and zoom the Moon or Mars and select locations to discover nearby landmarks and spacecraft. The planetary surfaces are illustrative 3D visualisations rather than official NASA terrain maps.

One of the main features is the AI-powered spacecraft chatbot. Users can select retired spacecraft such as Opportunity and Sojourner and ask questions about their missions. Each spacecraft responds in a conversational style based on its own mission information and personality. Supporting facts and source references are displayed with responses to help users understand where the information comes from. To make the experience suitable for different age groups, the website provides two reading levels for children aged 6-8 and 9-12. It also includes voice input, read aloud functionality and achievement badges. When the AI service is unavailable, built in fact based replies provide an alternative way to access information.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the frontend, with Three.js for 3D planetary visualisation. The backend uses Python and FastAPI, while LangChain manages the AI conversation workflow. Groq is the default AI provider, with Google Gemini and OpenAI available as alternative providers. NASA Image and Video Library is used to retrieve mission images, captions and related credits. The NASA Mars Rover Photos API is also supported for rover photography when the service is available and properly configured. GitHub is used for source code management and Render is used to host the application. No additional physical hardware is required because users can access the platform through a desktop or mobile browser.

The creative idea behind Echoes of Exploration is to give retired spacecraft a voice. Rather than simply reading about a rover or probe, users can interact with it as a character and learn about its journey through conversation. We believe this makes the history of space missions more memorable and gives younger users a reason to explore beyond the information presented on the screen.

Throughout development, the team considered ease of use, age-appropriate content, accessibility, scientific accuracy and security. The interface was designed to work across different screen sizes and the Progressive Web App features support offline access after the initial visit. Security measures include input limits, request rate limiting, restricted cross-origin access, output sanitisation and server-side API key protection. We also considered the reliability of AI responses by providing mission facts and displaying supporting sources. The sample mission facts and planetary landmark details still require individual checking against official references before they can be treated as fully verified information.

Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space science, support independent learning and help younger generations appreciate the achievements of historic space missions. By bringing maps, 3D exploration, mission information and AI conversations together in one platform, Echoes of Exploration offers another way for people to discover the history of space exploration.
